title: Luang Prabang
summary: Town in northern Laos on a Mekong peninsula. Capital of the kingdom of Lan Xang from 1353, it later became a separate kingdom's capital, then the royal and religious centre of Laos. Its blend of Lao and colonial architecture led to World Heritage inscription in 1995.

as_recorded.value: From 1353 Louangphrabang, then called Muong Swa, was the capital
The town was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1995.

importance.justification: Former royal and religious capital of Laos and a World Heritage town, but of regional rather than world-historical scope.

sources.title: Town of Luang Prabang - UNESCO World Heritage Centre

reviewer_note: Sources differ on timing: UNESCO says the town was capital of Lane Xang from the 14th to 16th century, Britannica gives 1353 and a court move to Vientiane around 1563. Start year taken from Britannica; end year is the 1995 inscription, an arbitrary endpoint. (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from UNESCO, Encyclopaedia Britannica; quotes machine-checked.)
